newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAKIA LIBERALISES SOME CAPITAL MOVEMENTS ABROAD.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAKIA LIBERALISES SOME CAPITAL MOVEMENTS ABROAD.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Monday lifted some restrictions on the movement of capital abroad as of December 1, as a further step toward the full convertibility of the Slovak crown,

In a statement, the ministry said the new measure covers capital tied to receiving and extending financial and commercial loans for goods and services and direct investments, and the purchase of real estate abroad.
The finance ministry said it had lifted the obligation for Slovaks to seek central bank approval for investments and extending loans with maturities of five and more years in OECD countries.
The move also permits Slovaks to accept loans from foreigner entities from OECD countries to pay for goods or services supplied by foreign-based subjects.

"These steps expedite, simplify and make cheaper many commercial activities of Slovak citizens because they enable them to obtain financing under more favourable credit conditions than in local banks," the finance ministry statement said.
Under current legislation all foreign loans must be approved by the NBS including any Slovak direct investments or loan activities abroad.

Slovak officials have said that they were seeking to bring fiancial regulations in line with the standards of the Paris-based club of industrialised nations, the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD).

Marian Jusko, vice governor of the National Bank of Slovakia (NBS), told an international financial conference last week that the "liberalisation of the foreign exchange regime is a part of our strategy in adjusting foreign exchange environment according to the OECD standards."
Slovakia is seeking to become a member of the OECD by 1997, after its neighbours, the Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary joined the organisation over the past two years.
